```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A names a specific payer: municipal IT departments, clerks and ADA coordinators. B states outright that it has 'no defined payer yet' and no evidence of any institutional buyer.",
    "A cites actual spending by real buyers in this exact category: Cole County paid $7,000 for Continual Engine in March 2026, and Templeton, MA was quoted $2,510 by CivicPlus/AudioEye. B's willingness to pay rests only on competitor list prices ($8–20/mo), and several of its competitors are free.",
    "A's demand comes from a dated federal mandate (April 2027 / April 2028 deadlines, per ADA.gov and the Federal Register). That gives a reason to buy now that B's discretionary consumer category does not have.",
    "A's unit economics fit a solo operator better. A single municipal sale at roughly $149/mo or a $900–$7,000 project can be won by direct outreach. At B's $8/mo price, the brief's own acquisition costs ($20–50 per user via ASO, roughly $3.76 CPA on Apple Search Ads) have to be recovered through retention the brief does not show.",
    "Both markets are crowded, but A's incumbents charge meaningful prices. B's include free products from well-backed teams (Noora is free and Stanford-backed), which squeezes what a new entrant can charge.",
    "Against A: municipal procurement is slow, which strains the 90-day goal. The deadline has already been pushed back once. The legal-documentation layer carries liability. A's two demand quotes also express frustration with the mandate, not intent to buy from a new vendor, and Cole County had already bought from an incumbent. These are real risks, but B's lack of any payer is the more basic gap."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's strongest-sounding demand signal, 'After 3 weeks of daily warmups, I just... do it now', is an App Store review selected for and shown on Convo's own marketing page. It is curated by a competitor, says nothing about willingness to pay, and does not support B's undefined target customer. The two Reddit quotes describe personal use or gaps in chatbots, not purchase intent.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A clearly wins on payer definition and evidence of real spending. However, neither brief shows that a solo vendor can get through municipal procurement or win a sale against entrenched incumbents within 90 days. A's timeline risk is real and largely untested in its brief."
}
```
